top_temples.name: Golden Temple (Sri Harmandir Sahib)
top_temples.deity: Sikh Gurdwara – seat of Sri Guru Granth Sahib
top_temples.location_note: The holiest Sikh shrine in the world, founded in 1574 by Guru Ram Das; upper floor covered in gold, serves a free langar to over 100,000 people daily.

top_temples.name: Durgiana Temple
top_temples.location_note: Hindu temple rebuilt in 1921 with architecture deliberately echoing the Golden Temple; especially vibrant during Navratri and Diwali.

top_temples.name: Ram Tirath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Traditionally the site of Valmiki's ashram, where Sita is said to have taken shelter and given birth to Luv and Kush; hosts a major annual fair.

top_temples.name: Mata Lal Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Modeled on the Vaishno Devi shrine, with a mirrored Sheesh Mahal sanctum and a man-made cave passage to the main shrine.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Temple, Amritsar
top_temples.location_note: Amritsar branch of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness.

top_temples.name: Gurdwara Singhwala Sahib
top_temples.location_note: One of the most visited historic shrines just outside Barnala town.

top_temples.name: Nanaksar Bahadur Gurudwara
top_temples.location_note: Large 11-acre complex in Barnala Tehsil, about 25 km from the main city.

top_temples.name: Gurudwara Sahib Arrisar Patshahi Nouvin
top_temples.location_note: Located in Handiaya village, 11 km from Barnala on the Mansa-Barnala Road.

top_temples.name: Geeta Bhawan
top_temples.location_note: Temple in the heart of Barnala city, managed by the Om Sat Sanatan Geeta Bhawan Trust.

top_temples.name: Kali Mata Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Prominent Devi temple in Barnala.

top_temples.name: Takht Sri Damdama Sahib
top_temples.location_note: One of the five Takhts (seats of Sikh temporal authority), in Talwandi Sabo about 28 km from Bathinda; where Guru Gobind Singh prepared the final Sri Guru Granth Sahib in 1705.

top_temples.name: Gurdwara Haji Rattan Sahib
top_temples.location_note: Located in the middle of Bathinda city, sharing a complex with the Sufi Mazaar of Peer Haji Rattan, reflecting interfaith harmony.

top_temples.name: Prachin Durga Mata Mandir
top_temples.location_note: One of the oldest temples in Bathinda city, known for its Shiv Parivar shrine and Shivling.

top_temples.name: Shri Panchmukhi Balaji Dham
top_temples.location_note: Popular Hanuman temple within Bathinda city.

top_temples.name: Chamunda Devi Ji Temple
top_temples.location_note: Well-known Devi temple in Bathinda.

top_temples.name: Gurudwara Nada Sahib
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Ghaggar river in Panchkula, about 15 km from Chandigarh; one of the tricity's most important Sikh shrines.

top_temples.name: Sri Karthikeya Swamy Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of Chandigarh's most notable Hindu temples.

top_temples.name: Gurdwara Sri Amb Sahib (Patshahi Satvi)
top_temples.location_note: Built around the mango tree where a devotee blessed by Guru Har Rai meditated.

top_temples.name: Chandi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: On the Chandigarh-Kalka road; the temple after which Chandigarh is popularly said to be named.

top_temples.name: Gurdwara Singh Sabha
top_temples.location_note: Known for its golden-and-white exterior, illuminated at night.

top_temples.name: Gurudwara Harisar Sahib
top_temples.location_note: Seven-story structure in Kot Fatuhi village, described as the tallest gurdwara in India.

top_temples.name: Gurudwara Harian Vellan Patshahi VII
top_temples.location_note: Located in Bajrour village near Hoshiarpur.

top_temples.name: Gurudwara Garna Sahib
top_temples.location_note: In Garhdiwala village, with a large prayer hall and sarovar.

top_temples.name: Kamahi Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: In Beh Nangal, believed to have been built by the Pandavas; one of Hoshiarpur's most famous temples.

top_temples.name: Gagan Ji Ka Tilla
top_temples.location_note: Ancient hilltop Shiv Mandir near Dasuya, reached via roughly 750 stairs.

top_temples.name: Devi Talab Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Nearly 200 years old, in the heart of Jalandhar; one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, with the shrine sited in the middle of a sacred pond.

top_temples.name: Sodal Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Located on Sodal Road near Devi Talab Mandir.

top_temples.name: Tulsi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: One of Jalandhar's well-known Hindu temples.

top_temples.name: Gurudwara Talhan Sahib Ji
top_temples.location_note: Major Sikh shrine in Talhan village near Jalandhar.

top_temples.name: Gurdwara Chhevin Padshahi
top_temples.location_note: In Basti Sheikh, marking a historic meeting between the Guru and a Muslim saint.

top_temples.name: Gurudwara Dukh Niwaran Sahib
top_temples.location_note: In the Field Ganj area; associated with a legend of Guru Nanak Dev curing a leper king.

top_temples.name: Gurdwara Sri Manji Sahib (Alamgir Sahib)
top_temples.location_note: In Alamgir village, where Guru Gobind Singh is said to have created a spring (Tirsar) with an arrow.

top_temples.name: Gurudwara Nanaksar Sahib
top_temples.location_note: On the Ludhiana-Malerkotla Road, dedicated to Guru Nanak Dev.

top_temples.name: Sheeshe Wala Gurudwara
top_temples.location_note: Notable for its architecture built entirely of glass.

top_temples.name: Shri Krishna Mandir
top_temples.location_note: One of Ludhiana's prominent Hindu temples.

top_temples.name: Gurudwara Nanaksar Sahib, Takhtupura
top_temples.location_note: Sanctified by visits from Guru Nanak Dev, Guru Hargobind Singh, and Guru Gobind Singh.

top_temples.name: Gurudwara Sahib Patsahi Pehli
top_temples.location_note: Six-story building with a large marble-floored hall, commemorating Guru Nanak Dev's visit.

top_temples.name: Gurudwara Bhatta Sahib
top_temples.location_note: Significant Sikh shrine in Moga drawing devotees region-wide.

top_temples.name: Shri Sanatam Dharam Hari Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Historic pilgrimage temple in Moga, especially busy on Tuesdays.

top_temples.name: Geeta Bhawan
top_temples.location_note: Temple located south of Moga city.

top_temples.name: Gurudwara Dukhnivaran Sahib
top_temples.location_note: Spread across seven acres; devotees visit believing it alleviates grief.

top_temples.name: Kali Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Built by the royal family of Patiala as a dedicated Hindu place of worship.

top_temples.name: Gurudwara Shri Khichri Sahib
top_temples.location_note: Located in Balbera village near Patiala.

top_temples.name: Gurudwara at Karhali
top_temples.location_note: In Karhali village, associated with Guru Hargobind Singh Ji.

top_temples.name: Gurudwara at Chitanwala
top_temples.location_note: In Nabha tehsil, marking Guru Nanak Dev's visit to Bhai Chanan Mal Ji.

top_temples.name: Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib
top_temples.deity: Sikh Takht – birthplace of the Khalsa
top_temples.location_note: One of the five Takhts of Sikhism; founded 1689, site where Guru Gobind Singh created the Khalsa Panth on Baisakhi 1699. Houses relics including a sword of Guru Gobind Singh.

top_temples.name: Gurdwara Qila Anandgarh Sahib
top_temples.location_note: One of the historic forts built by Guru Gobind Singh within Anandpur Sahib, distinct from Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib.
